research.title: Conformal Prediction Under Covariate Shift
bullets: Designed controlled experiments comparing split conformal and importance-weighted prediction intervals under simulated covariate shifts in regression datasets.
Analyzed coverage and interval width across feature subgroups, examining sensitivity to density ratio estimation and calibration sample composition.

research.title: Probability Calibration for Imbalanced Classification
bullets: Designed experiments comparing sigmoid and isotonic calibration for classifiers trained with class weighting and resampling on imbalanced tabular datasets.
Analyzed reliability diagrams, Brier scores, and stratified bootstrap intervals to assess calibration differences across prevalence settings and validation strategies.

publications.title: Validation Strategies for Probability Calibration in Imbalanced Tabular Classification

work.title: Batch Data Validation and Import Maintenance
bullets: Implemented Python validation routines for batch imports, checking required fields, duplicate records, and inconsistent value formats before database insertion.
Maintained regression tests for parsing failures and updated error reporting to support investigation of rejected records during routine imports.

projects.title: Missing Data Strategies for Tabular Prediction
bullets: Implemented preprocessing pipelines comparing median, nearest-neighbor, and iterative imputation before logistic regression and tree-based classification on tabular datasets.
Evaluated predictive performance under simulated missingness mechanisms, fitting imputers within training folds to prevent information leakage during cross-validation.

projects.title: Covariance Regularization for Discriminant Classification
bullets: Implemented discriminant classifiers using empirical, diagonal, and shrinkage covariance estimates, with shared preprocessing and cross-validation procedures for comparative evaluation.
Compared classification error and covariance conditioning across correlated feature settings, examining sensitivity to training sample size and regularization choices.
